title: Best workflow for rigging Meshy AI characters with separate clothes?
author: Miaou-Miaou1
selftext:
Hi everyone! I need some help figuring out the best workflow for creating and animating characters for my game.  
Right now I’m using Meshy AI to generate my 3D characters, but I’m having a lot of problems once I start rigging and animating them.  
When I generate the full character with clothes already on the body, everything looks fine at first. But once I add a skeleton/rig and start applying animations, the clothes can get badly distorted, stretched, twisted, or move strangely with the body.  
So I tried another approach:  
Generate the character/body first → rig and animate it → then add the clothes separately afterwards.  
The problem is that I don’t really know the correct way to attach the clothes afterwards so that they properly follow the character’s skeleton. The clothes sometimes move independently, clip through the body, deform badly, or just don’t follow the animations correctly.  
I also tried generating the clothes separately in Meshy, then importing them and putting them onto the character in Blender, but the results aren’t great either. Getting the clothes to properly fit the character and deform naturally during animations has been difficult.  
I’ve also been testing Cascadeur for animation/rigging. My character is already in a proper T-pose, but when I try using Cascadeur’s automatic posing/rigging tools, the result doesn’t seem very accurate and the skeleton doesn’t always fit the character properly.  
So I’m wondering what workflow people here would recommend.  
Is it better to:  
• Generate the character with the clothes already included, then rig everything together?  
• Create a base body, rig it first, and create/add the clothes afterwards?  
• Rig the clothes separately or transfer the character’s weights to the clothes?  
• Do most of this manually in Blender instead of relying on Meshy/Cascadeur auto-rigging?  
My final goal is to have one character with multiple outfits/accessories, so I don’t want to generate a completely new character every time I change clothes.  
If anyone is working with Meshy AI + Blender + Cascadeur, or has a good character → clothing → rig → animation workflow, I’d really appreciate some advice.  
I’m still learning this part of 3D development, so even a step-by-step explanation of your workflow would help a lot. Thanks!
